title: Egg white, omelet, scrambled, or fried, with meat

content.title: About
content.content: Egg white is the clear part of an egg, rich in high‑quality protein and virtually free of fat. When prepared as an omelet, scrambled, or fried with added meat, it combines the protein power of egg whites with the nutrients of meat such as iron, vitamin B12, and zinc.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg white provides about 10 g of protein per 100 g.
Unlike the yolk, egg white contains almost no cholesterol.
Heat denatures the proteins, making them more digestible.
Combining egg white with meat improves the bioavailability of amino acids.
Egg whites are a staple in sports nutrition for muscle recovery.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: The protein from egg whites and meat supplies all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Egg whites are virtually fat‑free, and using lean meat keeps the overall fat level low.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat adds vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The dish provides iron, zinc, and selenium, essential for immune function and blood formation.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of protein and a modest amount of fat promotes prolonged fullness.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white.

items.title: Processed meat concerns
items.content: Choose lean, minimally processed meats to avoid excess sodium and additives.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt or processed meat can raise sodium levels; monitor usage.

items.title: Cooking safety
items.content: Undercooked egg whites may harbor pathogens; cook until fully set.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Whisk egg whites with a splash of water, fold in diced lean meat (chicken, turkey, beef). Cook in a non‑stick pan with a little oil, stirring for scrambled eggs or letting it set for an omelet. Add vegetables and seasonings as desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh eggs in the refrigerator for up to 3 weeks. Cooked dishes should be consumed within 24 hours and kept in an airtight container in the fridge.
